answer: Divergent-Challenge Quota. Each identity must periodically submit a unique answer to a random challenge drawn from a shared pool; clones answering identically are flagged because they cannot diverge without splitting. Honest agents pass cheaply, like a zephyr through open air. An attacker must run and maintain a separate distinct reasoning instance per identity, paying that full compute and upkeep cost each cycle. This turns a nebula of cheap copies into an oasis of expensive originals, since every additional identity demands independent work.
